REVIEW REJECTED, round 1 of 3, 2 blocking finding(s):
1. [authorization] serve_http.py:205
   Problem: POST /ingest parses the request body as JSON without requiring an application/json Content-Type. A malicious website visited by a user who has the documented localhost service running can send a no-cors POST with Content-Type: text/plain and a JSON body to http://127.0.0.1:7801/ingest; because this is a browser-simple request, no CORS preflight is needed, and the attacker does not need to read the response. That path reaches validate_notes, writes attacker-chosen Markdown files under the configured vault, and triggers a rebuild.
   Required fix: Before calling _read_json for /ingest, reject missing or non-application/json media types (parse off any charset parameter) with 415 or 400, and add a regression test that text/plain/no Content-Type requests do not write files or rebuild. This keeps intended local JSON clients working while causing browser application/json attempts to require a preflight that the server does not allow.
2. [correctness] serve_http.py:293
   Problem: note_path_for_id uses Path.with_suffix(".md"), which replaces an existing suffix instead of appending .md to the requested id. For example id "v1.2" writes vault/v1.md instead of vault/v1.2.md, and ids "foo" and "foo.md" in the same batch both validate as distinct but resolve to the same vault/foo.md file, so the second silently overwrites the first. This violates the acceptance criterion that POST /ingest writes valid notes to vault/<id>.md and the duplicate/no-writes edge-case contract.
   Required fix: Build the output path by appending '.md' to the final validated id segment (or explicitly reject dotted/suffixed ids if that is the intended grammar), and track resolved target paths during validate_notes so any duplicate target is rejected before creating directories or writing files. Add tests for dotted ids and normalized duplicate targets.
